title: Optimal estimation of high-dimensional quantum states using locally gentle measurements
summary: We study the task of estimating a $d-$dimensional quantum state $ρ$ under the constraint that the measurement is $α-$gentle. Such measurements $M$ do not collapse the state; they issue both a random variable $R^M = ω$ containing statistical information and a post-measurement state $ρ_{M \to ω}$ such that $\|ρ_{M\to ω} - ρ\|_{Tr} \leq α$. We describe gentle measurements and their connection to quantum differential privacy.
